disease_label_per_paper: Pelvic inflammatory disease complicated by a tubo-ovarian abscess
presentation_summary: 47-year-old woman initially presented to primary care with 2 days of left lower quadrant and suprapubic pressure or burning.
She reported vaginal discharge, dysuria, chills, and nausea, and reported sex 1 month earlier with a partner who subsequently tested positive for chlamydia.
Office vital signs were afebrile and hemodynamically stable: temperature 96.9 F, blood pressure 119/82 mmHg, heart rate 98/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 97%.
Abdominal examination showed left lower quadrant and suprapubic tenderness; pelvic examination showed cervical motion tenderness.
Initial labs showed leukocytosis with WBC 17.69 x 10^3/uL and normal creatinine and liver enzymes.

When pelvic pain worsened 3 days later, CT showed a new left adnexal mass-like density with marked surrounding fat stranding and reactive inflammatory changes involving adjacent sigmoid colon and bladder, without diverticulitis.
Pelvic ultrasound showed a complex left adnexal cyst-like lesion with thick septations and surrounding hyperemia, measuring up to 7.4 x 5.5 cm and concerning for tubo-ovarian abscess.
